summary: Live sensitivity label propagation for SIEM enrichment and compliance playbook
description: Issue summary: Customer requests a documented and repeatable playbook plus signed evidence demonstrating how message-level sensitivity labels (e.g., PII, FINANCIAL, INTERNAL) are propagated through Redwood's audit pipeline into the SIEM enrichment stream and to downstream security consoles. Impact: FinSolve is onboarding Redwood for production inference and must provide auditors a mapping and proof that sensitivity labels applied at request ingestion are preserved, transformed, and tokenized appropriately in their SIEM (Splunk) environment. This affects their compliance acceptance (PCI/GLBA) and SOC2 controls. The customer is pausing go-live until proof is accepted by their InfoSec team. Environment: prod us-west tenant: finsolve-prod. Desired outcome: 1) A playbook describing labeling -> enrichment path, transformation rules, and examples. 2) A signed evidence bundle (sample events, checksums, mapping matrix, and timeline) demonstrating label propagation and that label tokens are never written to plaintext audit fields not allowed by their policy. 3) Config snippets for Splunk HEC ingestion and recommended header naming conventions. 4) Any required console or tenant-setting toggles and recommended RBAC settings.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer ingests sample requests with sensitivity metadata in the request headers (X-Redwood-Sensitivity: PII or FINANCIAL). 2) Submit generation and embedding requests from tenant finsolve-prod in us-west. 3) Observe audit event in Redwood audit stream and the downstream Splunk HEC index. 4) Verify that sensitivity label appears in expected enrichment field (siem.sensitivity_label) and that raw user content is redacted or pseudonymized per FinSolve's policy. 5) Check HMAC signatures for batch files and compare checksums to provided manifest.
logs: CloudWatch link: https://console.aws.amazon.com/cloudwatch/home?region=us-west-2#logsV2:log-groups/log-group:/aws/redwood/audit-stream/logs; sample audit event snippet: 2026-03-10T18:22:31Z tenant=finsolve-prod request_id=req_8a7c severity=INFO event_type=api.request labels=[PII] enrichment.si em.sensitivity_label=PII audit_manifest_checksum=sha256:3b2f... (full bundle attached privately). Splunk HEC sample line id: HEC-evt-20260310-00023 index: finsolve_audit field siem.sensitivity_label: "PII"; redacted_payload_hash: sha256:ab12...
request: Customer asks for: 1) A SIEM mapping matrix (Redwood audit field -> Splunk field -> allowed values) signed by Redwood support; 2) A short playbook (PDF) with step-by-step verification testers for FinSolve auditors; 3) Sample bundle with 5 real-world events (sanitized) and manifest + per-file checksums + HMAC proof and rotation metadata; 4) Confirmation of which tenant settings control label propagation and whether sensitive labels are included in audit payloads vs. enrichment headers; 5) Recommended RBAC for access to unredacted audit slices in case of legal hold.
investigation_notes: Initial triage: Support verified that incoming requests carried X-Redwood-Sensitivity headers and that audit events included labels field. SRE checked the enrichment path for the Splunk HEC connector and found a normalization stage that maps labels using a per-tenant mapping table (sensitive_label_map). That mapping table in finsolve-prod contains the expected keys but a prior migration (INT-4123) left an empty 'legacy_tokenization' flag on a subset of shards that can cause the enrichment to drop label context during batch export. Hypothesis: intermittent missing labels in downstream SIEM correlate to export shard migration windows. Evidence: export logs show 'legacy_tokenization=false' for shard s-34b in 2026-03-09T02:xx which aligns with FinSolve-reported misses. Next steps: 1) Produce mapping matrix and playbook draft for customer. 2) Re-run a controlled export with migration flags forced to 'true' to reproduce positive propagation. 3) Prepare signed bundle for auditor with manifest and HMAC keys rotated and attested by SRE. 4) Coordinate with Security for signed statement.
